_readme: A small HTML question set for trying out import and practice.
1. Open your space, go to Questions, then Import
2. Choose JSON, click 'Choose a file' and pick this file
3. Click 'Check the file' - nothing is written yet, you just see the report
5. Go back to the space and click 'Start practising'
It deliberately contains all five question formats, so practice shows you each
answer control in turn: multiple choice, multiple select, true/false, short
The subject is matched by name, case-insensitively, so 'HTML' below finds your
'Html' subject. No topics are named, because your curriculum has none yet - add
some later and you can re-import a version that uses them.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: Which element marks up the most important heading on a page?
questions.explanation: There should be one <h1> per page, describing what the page is about. <title> sets the browser tab text, <header> is a layout region, and <head> holds metadata rather than visible content.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: What does the alt attribute on an do?
questions.explanation: It gives a text alternative for people using a screen reader, and is displayed if the image fails to load. Purely decorative images should use alt="" so assistive technology skips them entirely.

options.text: Shows a tooltip when you hover the image
Describes the image for screen readers and when it fails to load
Sets the image width and height

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: Which attribute connects a <label> to the form control it describes?
questions.explanation: The label's for attribute must match the input's id. This makes clicking the label focus the field, and tells a screen reader what the field is for. Wrapping the input inside the label works too.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: Where should a <script> tag usually go for the best page-load experience?
questions.explanation: Scripts block HTML parsing while they download and run. Putting them just before </body>, or in <head> with the defer attribute, lets the browser render the page first.

options.text: At the very top of <head>, so it loads first
Just before </body>, or in <head> with defer
Inside the first <div> of the page
It makes no difference where it goes

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: Which input type gives a mobile user the most helpful keyboard for entering an email address?
questions.explanation: type="email" shows a keyboard with @ and . readily available, and turns on the browser's built-in format checking. There is no type="mail" or type="string".

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: Which of these are semantic HTML5 elements?
questions.explanation: article, nav and figure all describe what their content is. div and span are deliberately generic containers with no meaning, which is exactly why they should be a last resort.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: Which of these elements are self-closing (void) elements?
questions.explanation: img, br and input have no closing tag because they cannot contain content. p and div both wrap content and must be closed.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: A <div> tells the browser something about the meaning of its contents.
questions.explanation: False. A div is a generic container with no semantic meaning at all. Reach for header, nav, main, article, section, aside or footer when the content has an actual role.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.explanation: False. It is a document type declaration, not a tag. Its job is to tell the browser to use standards mode rather than the old quirks mode.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: An id must be unique within a single HTML document.
questions.explanation: True. Two elements may never share an id, even if they are different kinds of element. When several elements share a purpose, use a class instead.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: Client-side validation with the required attribute means you no longer need to validate on the server.
questions.explanation: False. Anyone can bypass the browser entirely and post directly to your server. Client-side validation is a convenience for honest users; server-side validation is the actual protection.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: Which attribute makes a form field compulsory, so the browser blocks submission while it is empty?
questions.explanation: The required attribute. The browser shows its own validation message and refuses to submit, though you still need to check the value on the server.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.stem: What prefix do you give a custom attribute so it is valid HTML and readable from JavaScript via the dataset property?
questions.explanation: Any attribute starting with data-. For example data-user-id becomes element.dataset.userId, with the hyphenated name converted to camelCase.

payload.front: What is the difference between a block-level element and an inline element?
payload.back:
A block-level element starts on a new line and takes up the full width available — div, p, h1, section.

An inline element sits within a line of text and takes only as much width as its content — span, a, strong, em.

payload.front: What are the four parts of a minimal HTML document, and what does each do?
payload.back:
1. <!DOCTYPE html> — puts the browser in standards mode.
2. <html> — the root element; carries the lang attribute.
3. <head> — metadata the user does not see: title, charset, viewport, stylesheets.
4. <body> — everything actually rendered on the page.
